  EGA (fe'ldan OLDIN):
    I     you    he    she   it
    we    you    they

  TUShUM (fe'l/predlogdan KEYIN):
    me    you    him   her   it
    us    you    them

  She is slim.  (ega - 'u')
  He loves her. (tushum - 'uni')

  ⚠ 'you' va 'it' ikkala ustunda
  BIR XIL.


⚠ O'ZBEKChA BILAN SOLIShTIRISh:

  sen → you / you

  biz → we / us

  ular → they / them

  → tushum)

Object pronouns: me, you, him, her, it, us, you, them — He loves her.

I don't play, he doesn't play, we don't play

topics.topic: Present Simple - Spelling, Use, Pronunciation — Present Simple - imlo, ishlatilishi, talaffuz (1)

topics.topic: Grammar: Present Simple - Present Continuous — Grammatika: Present Simple - Present Continuous
topics.rule_uz:
IKKI HOZIRGI ZAMON.


=== PRESENT SIMPLE ===

ShAKLI:
  I / you / we / they  + FE'L
  he / she / it        + FE'L + S

  I work.      He workS.
  We live.     She liveS.

INKOR:
  I don't work.   He doesn't work.
  ⚠ 'doesn't' dan keyin -S TUShADI!
  'He doesn't workS' - XATO.

SO'ROQ:
  Do you work?   Does he work?

⚠ 3-ShAXS BIRLIKDAGI -S QOIDALARI:
  work  → works
  go    → goes   (o, s, sh, ch, x dan
  watch → watches   keyin -ES)
  study → studies (undosh + y → -IES)
  play  → plays   (unli + y → faqat -S)
  have  → has     (istisno)

QAChON IShLATILADI:
  a) odat, kundalik ish
     'We spend our days hiking.'
  b) doimiy holat
     'Norwegians love the outdoors.'
  c) umumiy haqiqat
     'The sun rises in the east.'

BELGI SO'ZLARI:
  always, usually, often, sometimes,
  never, every day, on Mondays


=== PRESENT CONTINUOUS ===

ShAKLI:
  am / is / are + FE'L + ING

  I am working.
  He is working.
  We are working.

INKOR:
  I'm not working.
  He isn't working.

SO'ROQ:
  Are you working?
  Is he working?

⚠ -ING QO'ShISh QOIDALARI:
  work  → working
  make  → making   (oxirgi 'e' TUShADI)
  sit   → sitting  (qisqa unli + bitta
                    undosh → UNDOSh
                    IKKILANADI)
  lie   → lying    (-ie → -ying)

QAChON IShLATILADI:
  c) aynan hozir bo'layotgan ish
     'At the moment we are having a
      cup of hot chocolate.'
  e) shu davrda bo'layotgan ish
     'I'm having a fantastic time.'
  d) yaqin kelajakdagi ANIQ reja
     'Next week we're going to Oslo.'

BELGI SO'ZLARI:
  now, at the moment, right now,
  today, this week, look!, listen!


=== ENG MUHIM FARQ ===

  'I work in a bank.'
     = mening kasbim shu (DOIMIY)

  'I'm working in a bank.'
     = hozircha shu yerda ishlayapman
       (VAQTINChA)


=== HOLAT FE'LLARI (state verbs) ===

  Bu fe'llar CONTINUOUS shaklda
  IShLATILMAYDI:

  like, love, hate, want, need,
  know, understand, believe,
  remember, forget, mean,
  belong, own, cost, seem

  ⚠ 'I am loving' - XATO.
     'I love' - to'g'ri.

  ⚠ Betdagi 26-mashqda: 'Mr Harris
  NEEDS me' - 'is needing' EMAS.


⚠ 'HAVE' - IKKI XIL:

  EGALIK ma'nosida - continuous YO'Q:
     'I have a car.' ('I am having a
      car' - XATO)

  IBORALARDA - continuous BOR:
     'We are having a cup of hot
      chocolate.'
     'I'm having a fantastic time.'
     'We are having a meeting.'

  ⚠ Xatda ikkalasi ham uchraydi!
examples: Present Simple: I work. / He works.
Present Simple negative: I don't work. / He doesn't work.
Present Continuous: I am working. / He is working.
Present Simple is used for habits, routines and permanent states.
Present Continuous is used for actions happening now or around now.
Present Continuous is also used for fixed arrangements in the near future.
State verbs (like, love, know, need, want) are not used in the continuous.
'have' takes the continuous only in expressions: have a meeting, have a good time.

topics.topic: Adverbs of Frequency — Chastota ravishlari
topics.rule_uz:
ChASTOTA RAVIShLARI - QANChALIK
  TEZ-TEZ?

  100% always      = har doim
       usually     = odatda
       often       = tez-tez
       sometimes   = ba'zan
       occasionally = vaqti-vaqti
                      bilan
       rarely      = kamdan-kam
    0% never       = hech qachon


O'RNI - 3 QOIDA:

  1) ASOSIY FE'LDAN OLDIN:
     I NEVER work on Saturdays.
     She RARELY takes the train.
     He SOMETIMES goes to the
     cinema.

  2) YORDAMChI FE'LDAN KEYIN:
     Do you OFTEN watch TV?

  3) 'TO BE' DAN KEYIN:
     Tom is USUALLY late.


⚠ ENG KO'P XATO:

  'I work never' ✗
  'Tom usually is late' ✗
  → ravish 'to be' dan KEYIN.


⚠ 'NEVER' - INKOR:

  'I never work' - 'don't' KERAK
  EMAS ('I don't never work' ✗).
examples: always — usually — often — sometimes — occasionally — rarely — never
I never work on Saturdays. She rarely takes the train. He sometimes goes to the cinema. (before the main verb)
Do you often watch TV in the evening? (after the auxiliary verb)
Tom is usually late for school. (after the verb to be)

topics.topic: Past Simple — Past Simple (o'tgan oddiy zamon) (1)
topics.rule_uz:
PAST SIMPLE - ShAKLI.

  TASDIQ - HAMMA ShAXSDA BIR XIL:
    I / you / he / she / it / we /
    they WORKED
    ⚠ 3-shaxsda -s YO'Q!

  TO'G'RI fe'llar: + -ed
    work → worked
  NOTO'G'RI fe'llar: alohida shakl
    sing → sang, go → went, buy →
    bought (kitob oxiridagi jadval)

  SO'ROQ: DID + ega + fe'l ASOSIY
    shakli
    Did he PLAY football yesterday?
    Did he GO swimming last week?
    ⚠ 'Did he played' ✗ - 'did'
    bo'lsa fe'l o'zgarmaydi!

  INKOR: DIDN'T + fe'l asosiy
    shakli
    I didn't PLAY football.
    I didn't GO swimming.

  QISQA JAVOB:
    Did you get up early? - Yes, I
    DID. / No, I DIDN'T.


⚠ -ED FAQAT BIR JOYDA:

  Tasdiqda fe'lda (played);
  so'roq/inkorda 'did'da - fe'l
  asosiy shaklda.
examples: I worked — Did I work? — I didn't work (same for all persons)
I work - I worked (regular: -ed); I sing - I sang (irregular)
Did he play football yesterday? Did he go swimming last week?
I didn't play football yesterday. I didn't go swimming last week.
'Did you get up early?' 'Yes, I did.' 'Did he watch TV?' 'No, he didn't.'

topics.topic: Past Simple — Past Simple (o'tgan oddiy zamon) (2)
topics.rule_uz:
-ED IMLOSI - 3 QOIDA.

  1) -e BILAN TUGASA: + -d
     live → lived, love → loved

  2) UNDOSh + y: -y → -ied
     try → tried, study → studied
     ⚠ unli + y: play → played
     (o'zgarmaydi)

  3) UNDOSh + URG'ULI UNLI +
     UNDOSh: oxirgi undosh
     IKKILANADI
     stop → stoPPed, plan → plaNNed
     ⚠ visit → visited (urg'u
     birinchi bo'g'inda -
     ikkilanmaydi)
examples: verbs ending in -e: + -d — I live - I lived
consonant + y → -ied — I try - I tried
one stressed vowel between two consonants → double consonant + -ed — I stop - I stopped

topics.topic: Past Simple — Past Simple (o'tgan oddiy zamon) (3)
topics.rule_uz:
PAST SIMPLE QAChON:

  1) O'TMIShDA ANIQ VAQTDA bo'lgan /
     tugagan harakat:
     Lisa BOUGHT a house LAST
     YEAR. (Qachon? - o'tgan yili)

  2) O'TMIShDAGI TAKRORLANGAN
     harakat (endi yo'q):
     He usually PLAYED football in
     his free time. (endi
     o'ynamaydi)


VAQT SO'ZLARI (belgilar):

  yesterday - kecha
  last night / week / year / month
    - o'tgan ...
  a month / two years ago - ...
    oldin
  in 1964 - yilda

  Fleming discovered penicillin IN
  1928.


⚠ 'AGO' OXIRIDA:

  'two years ago' (ago two years
  ✗).
examples: Lisa bought a house last year. (When? Last year.) — definite time in the past
He usually played football in his free time. (but he doesn't play football anymore.) — repeated action in the past
yesterday, last night/week/year/month, two years ago, in 1964 — Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928.

topics.topic: Used to — Used to (ilgari ... edi)
topics.rule_uz:
USED TO - ILGARI ... EDI (ENDI
  YO'Q).

  ShAKL: used to + FE'L (asosiy)
  Hamma shaxsda BIR XIL:
    I / she / they USED TO drink

  Sarah USED TO drink a lot of
  coffee. (endi ichmaydi)

  SO'ROQ: Did + ega + USE to ...?
    Did Sarah USE to drink ...?
  INKOR: didn't + USE to
    Sarah DIDN'T USE to drink ...

  ⚠ Savol va inkorda 'USE' (-d
  SIZ)! 'didn't used to' ✗


PAST SIMPLE BILAN BIR XIL:

  He USED TO live in a flat.
  = He LIVED in a flat.
  (ma'no farqi yo'q)


⚠ 'USED TO' FAQAT O'TMISh:

  Hozirgi odat uchun 'use to' YO'Q
  - 'usually' ishlatiladi.
examples: Sarah used to drink a lot of coffee. (Sarah doesn't drink a lot of coffee anymore.)
Did Sarah use to drink a lot of coffee? — Sarah didn't use to drink a lot of coffee.
He used to live in a flat. ALSO: He lived in a flat. (no difference in meaning)

topics.topic: Agreeing - Disagreeing - So - Neither/Nor — Qo'shilish - qo'shilmaslik - So - Neither/Nor
topics.rule_uz:
QO'ShILISh VA QO'ShILMASLIK.

  1) TASDIQQA QO'ShILISh - 'men
     ham':
     SO + yordamchi fe'l + ega
     A: Jim lives in Warsaw.
     B: SO DO I.

  2) INKORGA QO'ShILISh - 'men
     ham (...masman)':
     NEITHER / NOR + yordamchi fe'l
     + ega
     A: Eve doesn't like going to
        the cinema.
     B: NEITHER DOES Ann. / NOR
        DOES Ann.

  3) QO'ShILMASLIK:
     ega + yordamchi fe'l
     A: I never walk to school.
     B: Oh really? I DO.
     A: I often go swimming.
     B: I DON'T.


⚠ YORDAMChI FE'L GAPGA QARAB:

  lives → do / does
  is → am / is / are
  can → can
  went → did
  A: I can swim. B: So can I.
  A: I went home. B: So did I.


⚠ SO'Z TARTIBI:

  'So do I' (So I do ✗) - fe'l
  egadan OLDIN.
examples: A: Jim lives in Warsaw. B: So do I. (agree with a positive sentence)
A: Eve doesn't like going to the cinema. B: Neither/Nor does Ann. (agree with a negative sentence)
A: I never walk to school. B: Oh really? I do. (disagree)
A: I often go swimming at weekends. B: I don't. (disagree)

topics.topic: Grammar: Past Simple - 'used to' — Grammatika: Past Simple - 'used to' (1)
topics.rule_uz:
KITOBDAGI 'USE' QUTISI.

  1) 'We use USED TO or the PAST SIMPLE
     to describe past habits and states
     which don't happen/exist any more.'

     I worked / used to work as a cleaner.
        (past habit)
     I didn't have / didn't use to have
     long hair.  (state)

  2) 'We use the PAST SIMPLE for an action
     which happened at a specific time
     in the past.'

     We WENT to the beach last Saturday.
     NOT: We used to go to the beach
          last Saturday.


⚠ ENG MUHIM QOIDA:

  ANIQ VAQT ko'rsatilgan bo'lsa
  ('last Saturday', 'in 1999',
  'yesterday') - FAQAT past simple.

  ⚠ 'used to' TAKRORLANGAN odat yoki
  UZOQ DAVOM ETGAN holat uchun.


'USED TO' NING ShAKLLARI:

  Tasdiq:  I used to work.
  Inkor:   I didn't USE to work.
           (⚠ 'used' emas, 'USE'!)
  So'roq:  Did you USE to work?
           (⚠ yana 'USE')

  ⚠ 'didn't used to' - keng tarqalgan
  XATO. 'did' allaqachon o'tgan
  zamonni ko'rsatgan.


⚠ 'USED TO' va 'BE USED TO' -
BUTUNLAY BOShQA:

  'I used to smoke.'
     = ilgari chekardim (endi yo'q)

  'I am used to smoking.'
     = chekishga o'rganib qolganman

  ⚠ Ikkinchisida 'be' bor va keyin
  -ING keladi!


PAST SIMPLE QANDAY YaSALADI:

  TO'G'RI FE'LLAR (regular): + -ED
     start → started
     enjoy → enjoyed
     live  → lived   ('e' bor, faqat -D)
     travel → travelled (Britaniyada
        'l' IKKILANADI)
     study → studied (undosh + y → -ied)

  NOTO'G'RI FE'LLAR (irregular):
     be    → was/were
     go    → went
     sing  → sang
     have  → had
     learn → learnt (yoki learned)

  ⚠ Noto'g'ri fe'llar ro'yxati kitob
  oxirida (128-bet).


⚠ -ED NING TALAFFUZI - UCh XIL:

  /t/  - jarangsizdan keyin: worked,
         watched, finished
  /d/  - jaranglidan keyin: lived,
         enjoyed, travelled
  /id/ - 't' yoki 'd' dan keyin:
         started, needed, wanted

  ⚠ Bu 7-unitning talaffuz mavzusi.
examples: We use used to or the past simple to describe past habits and states which don't happen/exist any more.
I worked / used to work as a cleaner. (past habit)
I didn't have / didn't use to have long hair. (state)
We use the past simple for an action which happened at a specific time in the past.
We went to the beach last Saturday. NOT: We used to go to the beach last Saturday.

topics.topic: Grammar: Past Simple - 'used to' — Grammatika: Past Simple - 'used to' (2)
topics.rule_uz:
'THEN' VA 'NOW' - O'ZGARISh.

KITOBDAGI NAMUNA:
  'Pauline used to have short orange
   hair, but now she's got long brown
   hair.'

  ⚠ Qolip: used to + FE'L, but now +
     PRESENT.


THEN (rasmdagi yorliqlar):
  short orange hair - kalta to'q sariq soch
  glasses - ko'zoynak
  brightly coloured T-shirts - yorqin
     rangli futbolkalar
  ripped jeans - yirtiq jinsi

NOW (qaydlar):
  * ⚠ hair: long, ... (rangi audiodan)
  eyes: contact lenses
  * ⚠ clothes: smart ... (qanaqa - audiodan)
  habits: not smoke any more


⚠ 'USED TO BE LIKE':

  'what Pauline used to BE LIKE'
  = Polina qanday ODAM/QANDAY
    KO'RINIShDA bo'lgan.

  ⚠ 'be like' - 6-betdagi 2-mashqda
  o'rganilgan edi.


⚠ 'GLASSES' va 'CONTACT LENSES':

  glasses - ko'zoynak (HAR DOIM KO'PLIK)
  contact lenses - kontakt linzalar
     ⚠ 'a lens' → 'lenses'


⚠ 'RIPPED JEANS':

  'to rip' = yirtmoq
  → 'ripped' = yirtilgan
  ⚠ 'jeans' HAR DOIM KO'PLIKDA
  (trousers, shorts kabi).


⚠ 'SMART':

  Britaniyada 'smart' = OZODA, chiroyli
  kiyingan.
  ⚠ AQShda 'smart' = AQLLI.
  ⚠ Britaniyada aqlli - 'clever'.


⚠ 'NOT ... ANY MORE':

  'She doesn't smoke ANY MORE.'
  = U endi chekmaydi.

  ⚠ 'any more' (ikki so'z) - Britaniya;
  'anymore' (bir so'z) - AQSh.


⚠ GAP TUZISh QOLIPI:

  'She used to ... , but now she ... '
  yoki
  'She didn't use to ... , but now
   she ... '
examples: THEN: short orange hair. NOW: long, ... hair.
THEN: glasses. NOW: contact lenses.
THEN: brightly coloured T-shirts and ripped jeans. NOW: smart ... clothes.
NOW habits: she does not smoke any more.
Pauline used to have short orange hair, but now she's got long brown hair.

topics.topic: Grammar: Present Simple — Grammatika: Present Simple
topics.rule_uz:
KITOBDAGI 'USE' QUTISI.

  'We use the present simple to talk
   about daily routines and habits.'
  e.g. He goes to work by bus.

  ⚠ 'e.g.' = 'exempli gratia' (lotincha)
  = masalan.


⚠ 'BY BUS' - TRANSPORT USULI:

  by bus, by car, by train, by plane,
  by bike, by taxi

  ⚠ ARTIKLSIZ! 'by a bus' - XATO.
  ⚠ ISTISNO: 'ON FOOT' = piyoda
  ('by foot' XATO).


3-ShAXS BIRLIKDAGI -S QOIDALARI
(10-mashqning butun mavzusi):

  1) Ko'pchilik fe'lga oddiy -S:
     play → plays, read → reads,
     make → makes, leave → leaves

  2) -O, -S, -SH, -CH, -X bilan
     tugasa → -ES:
     go → goes, do → does,
     watch → watches, finish → finishes,
     brush → brushes, fix → fixes

  3) UNDOSh + Y → -IES:
     study → studies, fly → flies

  4) UNLI + Y → faqat -S:
     play → plays, buy → buys

  5) ISTISNO: have → HAS


⚠ -S NING TALAFFUZI - UCh XIL:

  /s/  - jarangsiz tovushdan keyin:
     makes, sleeps, works
  /z/  - jarangli tovushdan keyin:
     plays, reads, goes
  /iz/ - shivirlovchi tovushdan keyin:
     watches, finishes, brushes

  ⚠ Bu qoida ko'plik -S ga ham,
  o'tgan zamon -ED ga ham o'xshash.
examples: We use the present simple to talk about daily routines and habits.
e.g. He goes to work by bus.

topics.topic: Adjectives — Sifatlar
topics.rule_uz:
SIFAT - OTNI TASVIRLAYDI.

  1) BIRLIK VA KO'PLIKDA BIR XIL:
     a RED car - two RED cars
     ⚠ 'reds cars' ✗ - sifatga -s
     qo'shilmaydi!

  2) OTDAN OLDIN:
     a LARGE box (box large ✗)

  3) 'TO BE' VA HIS FE'LLARIDAN
     KEYIN YOLG'IZ:
     Mary IS tall.
     You LOOK sad.
     It SMELLS horrible.
     (look, smell, sound, feel,
     taste)


IKKI XIL SIFAT:

  FIKR (opinion) - odam nima deb
    o'ylaydi: beautiful, lovely,
    great, expensive
  FAKT (fact) - haqiqiy ma'lumot:
    short (o'lcham), square (shakl),
    yellow (rang), cotton (material)


⚠ O'ZBEKChA BILAN O'XShASh:

  'qizil mashina' - sifat otdan
  oldin, ko'plikda o'zgarmaydi -
  inglizcha ham shunday.
examples: a red car - (two) red cars (same form in singular and plural)
a large box (adjectives go before nouns)
Mary is tall. You look sad. It smells horrible. (after to be, look, smell, sound, feel, taste)
opinion adjectives: beautiful, lovely, great, expensive — fact adjectives: short, square, yellow, cotton

topics.topic: Order of Adjectives — Sifatlar tartibi
topics.rule_uz:
SIFATLAR TARTIBI.

  FIKR → FAKT:
    a BEAUTIFUL (fikr) SILK (fakt)
    scarf

  FAKT SIFATLARI TARTIBI:
    1 O'LChAM   small, big, short,
                long
    2 OG'IRLIK  heavy, light
    3 ShAKL     triangular, round,
                rectangular, square
    4 RANG      dark/light blue,
                yellow, pink, cream,
                red, purple
    5 MATERIAL  cotton, leather,
                silk, plastic,
                woollen, nylon,
                metal, gold, silver,
                velvet, wooden,
                canvas, china

  an EXPENSIVE (fikr), RED (rang),
  LEATHER (material) suitcase

  ⚠ Odatda 2-3 sifatdan ko'p
  ishlatilmaydi.


⚠ 'CHINA':

  = chinni (material); China =
  Xitoy.


⚠ 'LIGHT':

  = yengil (og'irlik) YOKI och
  (rang): light blue = och ko'k.
examples: a beautiful silk scarf (opinion before fact)
size → weight → shape → colour → material
an expensive, red, leather suitcase

topics.topic: Comparisons — Qiyoslash darajalari
topics.rule_uz:
QIYOSLASh - 3 DARAJA.

  ODDIY → QIYOSIY (-roq) →
  ORTTIRMA (eng)

  1) BIR BO'G'INLI: -er / the -est
     cheap → cheapER → the
       cheapEST
     large → largER → the largEST
       (-e bor - faqat -r/-st)
     big → biGGer → the biGGest
       (undosh ikkilanadi)

  2) -Y BILAN TUGAYDIGAN: -y → -ier
     / the -iest
     easy → easIER → the easIEST

  3) IKKI+ BO'G'INLI: more / the
     most
     intelligent → MORE intelligent
       → THE MOST intelligent

  4) NOTO'G'RI (yodlash):
     good → better → the best
     bad → worse → the worst
     much/many → more → the most
     little → less → the least
     far → further/farther → the
       furthest/farthest


⚠ ORTTIRMADA 'THE' ShART:

  'the cheapest' (cheapest ✗).


⚠ 'MORE CHEAPER' ✗:

  Yo -er, yo more - ikkalasi emas.
examples: cheap - cheaper - the cheapest; large - larger - the largest; big - bigger - the biggest (one syllable)
easy - easier - the easiest (-y adjectives)
intelligent - more intelligent - the most intelligent (two or more syllables)
good - better - the best; bad - worse - the worst; much/many - more - the most; little - less - the least; far - further/farther - the furthest/farthest

topics.topic: Comparisons - Form and Use — Qiyoslash - shakli va ishlatilishi (1)
topics.rule_uz:
QIYOSLASh ShAKLI - IMLO.

  1) BIR BO'G'INLI: + -er / -est
     cheap → cheaper → the cheapest
     large → largER → the largEST
     (-e bor: faqat -r / -st)

  2) UNDOSh + UNLI + UNDOSh:
     ikkilanadi
     big → biGGer → the biGGest
     hot → hoTTer → the hoTTest

  3) UNDOSh + -y: -y → -ier / -iest
     heavy → heavIER → the heavIEST
     easy → easier → the easiest

  4) IKKI+ BO'G'INLI: more / the
     most
     careful → MORE careful → THE
     MOST careful

  5) NOTO'G'RI: good/better/best
     ...


ESLATMA:

  Qiyosiy + THAN: bigger THAN
  Orttirma + THE: THE biggest
  Orttirma + OF / IN: the biggest
  IN the world / OF all
examples: large - larger (than) - the largest (of/in); cheap - cheaper - the cheapest
big - bigger - the biggest (double the last consonant)
heavy - heavier - the heaviest (-y → -ier/-iest)
careful - more careful - the most careful (two or more syllables)
than (comparative) — the (superlative)

topics.topic: Comparisons - Form and Use — Qiyoslash - shakli va ishlatilishi (2)
topics.rule_uz:
QIYOSLASh - 5 XIL QOLIP.

  1) QIYOSIY + THAN (ikki narsa):
     Sue's skirt is LONGER THAN
     Mary's.

  2) THE + ORTTIRMA + OF/IN (butun
     guruh):
     Pluto is THE COLDEST planet IN
     our solar system.

  3) (NOT) AS + SIFAT + AS (bir
     xil / bir xil emas):
     Tom is AS TALL AS Peter.
     Peter is NOT AS TALL AS Sally.

  4) LESS + SIFAT + THAN (kamroq):
     The green jacket is LESS
     EXPENSIVE THAN the yellow one.

  5) MUCH + QIYOSIY + THAN (ancha):
     This tie is MUCH LONGER THAN
     that one.


⚠ 'MARY'S' = Mary's skirt:

  Takrorlamaslik uchun egalik
  shakli yolg'iz qoladi.
examples: Sue's skirt is longer than Mary's. (comparative + than: two things)
Pluto is the coldest planet in our solar system. (superlative: whole group)
Tom is as tall as Peter. ((not) as ... as: similar / not similar)
The green jacket is less expensive than the yellow jacket. (less + adjective + than)
This tie is much longer than that one. (much + comparative + than)

topics.topic: Expressing Certainty: Must - Can't — Ishonch ifodasi: Must - Can't
topics.rule_uz:
IShONChLI TAXMIN - MUST / CAN'T.

  MUST + fe'l = bo'lsa kerak
    (mantiqan TO'G'RI - dalil bor)
    They look the same. They MUST
    BE twins.

  CAN'T + fe'l = bo'lishi mumkin
    emas (mantiqan NOTO'G'RI)
    This book CAN'T BE his. He
    doesn't like detective stories.

  ⚠ Bu yerda 'must' - majburiyat
  EMAS, taxmin. 'can't' -
  qobiliyat EMAS, taxmin.

  ⚠ Inkori 'mustn't' EMAS - 'can't'!
  (mustn't = taqiq)
examples: They look the same. They must be twins. (logically true)
This book can't be his. He doesn't like detective stories. (logically untrue)

topics.topic: Will (predictions) — Will (bashorat)
topics.rule_uz:
WILL - BAShORAT (fikrga
  asoslangan).

  I THINK he WILL help me.
  I EXPECT it will rain.
  He will PROBABLY come.

  Belgi so'zlar: think, expect,
  probably, I'm sure, perhaps.

  ⚠ will + fe'l ASOSIY shakli
  (will to help ✗, will helps ✗).
  ⚠ Qisqa: I'll, he'll; inkor:
  won't.
examples: I think he will help me. (prediction based on what we think)

topics.topic: Grammar: Order of Adjectives — Grammatika: Sifatlar tartibi (1)
topics.rule_uz:
KITOBDAGI QUTI.


1) SIFAT OTNI TASVIRLAYDI:

  'Adjectives describe nouns. They have
   the same form in the singular and
   plural.'

  e.g. a blue dress - two blue dresses

  ⚠ ENG MUHIM FARQ: ingliz sifati
  KO'PLIKDA O'ZGARMAYDI.
  ⚠ 'two blueS dresses' - XATO.


2) IKKI TUR SIFAT:

  OPINION (fikr) adjectives:
     beautiful, great, expensive, nice
     = biz NIMA DEB O'YLAYMIZ

  FACT (haqiqat) adjectives:
     short, long, red, wooden
     = narsa ASLIDA QANDAY

  ⚠ QOIDA: OPINION sifati FACT
  sifatidan OLDIN turadi.

  'She's wearing a BEAUTIFUL RED dress.'
     (opinion) (fact)

  ⚠ 'a red beautiful dress' - XATO.


3) FACT SIFATLARINING TARTIBI:

  size     - small, big, short, long
  weight   - heavy, light
  shape    - triangular, round,
             rectangular, square
  colour   - dark/light blue, yellow,
             pink, cream, red, purple
  material - cotton, leather, silk,
             plastic, woollen, nylon,
             metal, gold, silver, velvet,
             wooden, canvas

  ⚠ KITOBDAGI NAMUNA:
  "It's a beautiful, long, light blue,
   silk skirt."
     beautiful - OPINION
     long      - SIZE
     light blue - COLOUR
     silk      - MATERIAL


⚠ QISQA ESLATMA (yodlash uchun):

  FIKR → O'LChAM → OG'IRLIK →
  ShAKL → RANG → MATERIAL → OT

  ⚠ O'zbekchada bunday qat'iy tartib
  yo'q - shuning uchun bu qoidani
  ataylab yodlash kerak.


⚠ VERGUL QO'YILADIMI:

  Kitobdagi namunada vergul bor:
  'a beautiful, long, light blue, silk
   skirt'
  ⚠ Vergulsiz ham to'g'ri:
  'a beautiful long light blue silk
   skirt'
  ⚠ Amalda 2-3 tadan ortiq sifat kam
  ishlatiladi.


⚠ MATERIAL SIFATLARI - OTDAN:

  gold, silver, metal, plastic, silk,
  cotton, velvet, canvas - bular OT,
  lekin sifat vazifasida ishlatiladi.

  ⚠ Ba'zilari -EN oladi:
     wood → wooden
     wool → woollen
     gold → golden (ko'chma ma'noda)

  ⚠ 'a gold ring' = oltindan uzuk
  ⚠ 'a golden opportunity' = oltin
     imkoniyat (ko'chma)
examples: Adjectives describe nouns. They have the same form in the singular and plural. e.g. a blue dress - two blue dresses
Opinion adjectives (beautiful, great, expensive) describe what we think of someone or something.
Fact adjectives (short, long, red) describe what someone or something really is.
Opinion adjectives go before fact adjectives. She's wearing a beautiful red dress.
size: small, big, short, long, etc
weight: heavy, light, etc
shape: triangular, round, rectangular, square, etc
colour: dark/light blue, yellow, pink, cream, red, purple, etc

topics.topic: Grammar: Order of Adjectives — Grammatika: Sifatlar tartibi (2)
topics.rule_uz:
19-BETDAGI MAQOLADAN.


FACT ADJECTIVES (haqiqat) - misollar:

  large (department stores) - o'lcham
  small (antique shops)    - o'lcham
  little (streets)         - o'lcham
  woollen (skirts)         - material
  leather (jackets)        - material
  big (bank accounts)      - o'lcham

  ⚠ Bularni O'LChASh yoki KO'RISh
  mumkin.


OPINION ADJECTIVES (fikr) - misollar:

  delightful (smaller shops)
  fantastic (furniture)
  great (department stores / variety)
  rare (books)
  trendiest (boutiques)
  fashionable (clothes)

  ⚠ Bular bir odamga to'g'ri, boshqasiga
  noto'g'ri tuyulishi mumkin.


⚠ 'HIGH QUALITY' - QAYSI TUR:

  'high quality woollen skirts'
  ⚠ 'high quality' bu yerda OT+OT
  birikmasi bo'lib, sifat vazifasida.
  Uni ham FIKR sifatiga yaqin deb
  hisoblash mumkin.


⚠ 'RARE' - CHEGARADAGI SO'Z:

  'a rare book' - kitobning kam
  uchrashi HAQIQAT, lekin 'noyob'
  deyish BAHO ham beradi.

  ⚠ Bunday chegaradagi so'zlar bor -
  muhimi, tartibni to'g'ri qo'yish.
examples: FACT: large department stores
FACT: small antique shops
FACT: woollen skirts, leather jackets
OPINION: delightful smaller shops
OPINION: fantastic furniture
OPINION: the trendiest boutiques, fashionable clothes

topics.topic: Grammar: Making Comparisons — Grammatika: Qiyoslash
topics.rule_uz:
SIFATNING UCh DARAJASI.

  1) ODDIY (positive):    big
  2) QIYoSIY (comparative): biggER THAN
  3) ENG YUQORI (superlative):
     THE biggEST


QANDAY YaSALADI - UZUNLIGIGA QARAB:

  QISQA SIFATLAR (bir bo'g'inli va
  ba'zi ikki bo'g'inli):
     + -ER / THE + -EST

     short  → shorter  → the shortest
     long   → longer   → the longest
     cheap  → cheaper  → the cheapest

  UZUN SIFATLAR (ikki va undan ko'p
  bo'g'inli):
     MORE + sifat / THE MOST + sifat

     expensive → more expensive →
        the most expensive
     beautiful → more beautiful →
        the most beautiful


⚠ IMLO QOIDALARI (qisqa sifatlar):

  1) 'E' bilan tugasa - faqat -R/-ST:
     large → larger → the largest
     nice  → nicer  → the nicest

  2) QISQA UNLI + BITTA UNDOSh →
     UNDOSh IKKILANADI:
     big → biGGer → the biGGest
     hot → hoTTer → the hoTTest
     thin → thiNNer → the thiNNest

  3) UNDOSh + Y → -IER/-IEST:
     easy → easier → the easiest
     happy → happier → the happiest
     trendy → trendier → the trendiest


⚠ QOIDASIZ ShAKLLAR - YoDLASh ShART:

  good   → better  → the best
  bad    → worse   → the worst
  little → less    → the least
  much/many → more → the most
  far    → further/farther →
           the furthest/farthest

  ⚠ Jadvalda 'good', 'bad', 'little'
  aynan shu qoidasizlar.


⚠ 'THAN' va 'THE':

  QIYoSIYda 'THAN':
     'cheaper THAN the brown skirt'
  ENG YUQORIda 'THE':
     'THE cheapest skirt'

  ⚠ 'more cheaper' - XATO (ikki marta
  qiyoslash).
  ⚠ 'the most cheapest' - XATO.


⚠ KUChAYTIRUVChI SO'ZLAR:

  MUCH cheaper = ancha arzonroq
  FAR more expensive = ancha qimmatroq
  A LOT bigger = ancha kattaroq
  A BIT longer = biroz uzunroq

  ⚠ 'VERY cheaper' - XATO!
  'very' faqat ODDIY sifat bilan.


⚠ TENGLIK VA TENGSIZLIK:

  AS ... AS = ... dek
     'as nice as' = shunchalik chiroyli
  NOT AS ... AS = ... dek emas
     'not as long as' = shunchalik uzun
     emas
  THE SAME ... AS = bir xil
     'the same price as' = bir xil narxda

  ⚠ 22-mashqdagi ro'yxatda uchalasi
  ham bor.


⚠ 'LESS' - QIYoSIYNING AKSI:

  'less expensive' = kamroq qimmat
  = 'cheaper' bilan bir xil ma'no,
  lekin muloyimroq.
examples: Short adjectives: short - shorter than - the shortest
Long adjectives: expensive - more expensive than - the most expensive
big - bigger than - the biggest (the consonant doubles)
large - larger than - the largest (only -r/-st after 'e')
good - better than - the best
bad - worse than - the worst
little - less than - the least
as ... as / not as ... as / the same ... as

topics.topic: Adjectives - Adverbs — Sifat va ravish (1)
topics.rule_uz:
SIFAT va RAVISh - FARQI.

  SIFAT → OTni tasvirlaydi:
    a SMALL village
  RAVISh → FE'Lni (yoki sifat/
    ravishni) tasvirlaydi:
    He works HARD.
    He runs VERY fast.
    She is EXTREMELY polite.


-ING va -ED SIFATLAR:

  -ING = narsa QANDAY (sabab):
    The film was BORING.
    She is an INTERESTING person.
  -ED = odam QANDAY HIS QILADI
    (natija):
    The children were TERRIFIED.
    I'm BORED. (zerikdim)

  ⚠ 'I'm boring' = men zerikarli
  odamman! 'I'm bored' = zerikdim.


RAVISh O'RNI:

  Fe'ldan KEYIN: She spoke SOFTLY.
  Chastota ravishi fe'ldan OLDIN:
    He ALWAYS drives carefully.
examples: We live in a small village. (adjectives describe nouns)
The film was boring. She is a very interesting person. (-ing: what somebody/something is like)
The children were terrified when they heard the thunder. (-ed: how somebody feels)
He works hard. He runs very fast. She is extremely polite. (adverbs describe verbs, adverbs, adjectives)
She spoke softly. He always drives carefully. (position of adverbs)

topics.topic: Adjectives - Adverbs — Sifat va ravish (2)
topics.rule_uz:
RAVISh YASASh - SIFAT + -LY.

  1) ODDIY: + -ly
     dangerous → dangerousLY
     slow → slowly

  2) -LE: -e → -y
     gentle → gentLY
     terrible → terribly

  3) UNDOSh + Y: -y → -ily
     easy → easILY
     happy → happily

  4) -L: + -ly (ikkita l!)
     wonderful → wonderfulLY
     careful → carefully


MAXSUS ShAKLLAR:

  good → WELL (butunlay boshqa)
  fast → fast    (bir xil)
  hard → hard    (bir xil)
  early → early  (bir xil)
  late → late    (bir xil)

  ⚠ 'He runs fastly' ✗ → 'fast'.
  ⚠ 'hardly' = deyarli emas
  (boshqa ma'no!); 'lately' =
  yaqinda.


⚠ -LY BILAN TUGAYDIGAN SIFATLAR:

  friendly, lively, lonely, lovely,
  silly, ugly - bular RAVISh EMAS:
  He's a FRIENDLY person.
examples: dangerous - dangerously (+ -ly)
gentle - gently (-le → -ly)
easy - easily (consonant + y → -ily)
wonderful - wonderfully (-l + -ly)
good → well; fast → fast; hard → hard; early → early; late → late
friendly, lively, lonely, lovely, silly, ugly = adjectives (He's a friendly person.)

topics.topic: Past Continuous — Past Continuous (o'tgan davomli zamon)
topics.rule_uz:
PAST CONTINUOUS = was / were +
  fe'l-ING.

  TASDIQ:
    I / he / she / it WAS eating
    we / you / they WERE eating

  SO'ROQ (was/were oldinga):
    WAS he eating?
    WERE they eating?

  INKOR:
    I WASN'T eating
    they WEREN'T eating

  QISQA JAVOB:
    Was he eating? - Yes, he WAS. /
    No, he WASN'T.
    Were they eating? - Yes, they
    WERE. / No, they WEREN'T.


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  'yeyayotgan edi' = was eating.
  O'tmishda MA'LUM PAYTDA davom
  etayotgan harakat.

  ⚠ Ishlatilishi keyingi betda
  (21-bet).
examples: I / he / she / it was eating — we / you / they were eating
Was he eating? — Were they eating?
I wasn't eating — they weren't eating
Was he ...? — Yes, he was. / No, he wasn't. — Were they ...? — Yes, they were. / No, they weren't.

topics.topic: Past Continuous - Form and Use — Past Continuous - shakli va ishlatilishi
topics.rule_uz:
PAST CONTINUOUS QAChON - 4 HOLAT.

  1) O'TMIShDA MA'LUM PAYTDA davom
     etayotgan harakat:
     At five o'clock yesterday I
     WAS COOKING dinner.
     (boshi-oxiri noma'lum)

  2) UZUN HARAKAT + QISQA UZILISh:
     She WAS HAVING breakfast
     (uzun - Continuous)
     when the phone RANG
     (qisqa - Simple)

  3) BIR VAQTDA IKKI HARAKAT:
     Tina WAS DOING the washing-up
     WHILE the children WERE
     PLAYING in the garden.

  4) HIKOYADA FON:
     The sun WAS SHINING brightly
     AS Tom WAS DRIVING his brand
     new car ...


BOG'LOVChILAR:

  while / as + Past Continuous
    (uzun)
  when + Past Simple (qisqa)

  ⚠ 'when' + Continuous ham
  mumkin: 'When I was cooking,
  ...'


⚠ 'BRAND NEW':

  = yap-yangi.
examples: I was working. They were working. — Was he working? They weren't working.
At five o'clock yesterday I was cooking dinner. (action in progress at a stated time)
She was having breakfast when the phone rang. (longer action interrupted by shorter action)
Tina was doing the washing-up while the children were playing in the garden. (simultaneous actions)
The sun was shining brightly as Tom was driving his brand new car through the city centre. (background in a story)
while, when, as

topics.topic: Grammar: Adjectives - Adverbs — Grammatika: Sifat va ravish
topics.rule_uz:
KITOBDAGI 'USE' QUTISI.

  'ADJECTIVES describe NOUNS.
   ADVERBS usually describe VERBS or
   other adverbs.'

  'She was holding a bouquet of PRETTY
   flowers.'  (sifat + ot)
  '"Excuse me," the young woman said
   SWEETLY.'  (fe'l + ravish)


⚠ ASOSIY FARQ:

  SIFAT → QANDAY? (ot haqida)
     'a pretty flower' - qanday gul?

  RAVISh → QANDAY QILIB? (fe'l haqida)
     'she said sweetly' - qanday aytdi?


⚠ RAVISh QANDAY YaSALADI:

  SIFAT + -LY:
     sweet → sweetly
     soft  → softly
     loud  → loudly
     heavy → heavily (undosh + y → -ily)
     terrible → terribly ('-le' → '-ly')


⚠ QOIDASIZ RAVIShLAR:

  good → WELL   (⚠ 'goodly' XATO)
  fast → fast   (o'zgarmaydi)
  hard → hard   (o'zgarmaydi)
  late → late   (o'zgarmaydi)
  early → early (o'zgarmaydi)

  ⚠ 'hardly' MAVJUD, lekin ma'nosi
  BOShQA: 'deyarli emas'.
     'He works HARD.' = qattiq ishlaydi
     'He HARDLY works.' = deyarli
        ishlamaydi

  ⚠ 'lately' ham boshqa ma'noda:
  'so'nggi paytlarda'.


⚠ -LY BILAN TUGAGAN SIFATLAR:

  friendly, lovely, lonely, silly,
  ugly, likely

  ⚠ Bular SIFAT, ravish EMAS!
  ⚠ Ulardan ravish yasash uchun
  'in a ... way' ishlatiladi:
  'in a friendly way'.


⚠ HIS FE'LLARIDAN KEYIN SIFAT:

  be, look, seem, sound, feel, taste,
  smell, become, get

  ⚠ Bulardan keyin SIFAT keladi,
  ravish EMAS:
     'She looks BEAUTIFUL.'
        ('beautifully' XATO)
     'It sounds GOOD.' ('well' XATO)
     'The food tastes DELICIOUS.'

  ⚠ Hikoyada: 'You LOOK as if ...',
  'It SOUNDS like ...'


⚠ HIKOYaDAGI RAVIShLAR:

  heavily  - qattiq (yomg'ir)
  sweetly  - shirin ohangda
  jokingly - hazillashib
  loudly   - baland ovozda
  softly   - ohista
  still    - hamon
  no longer - endi ... emas
examples: Adjectives describe nouns.
Adverbs usually describe verbs or other adverbs.
She was holding a bouquet of pretty flowers.
"Excuse me," the young woman said sweetly.
good → well (irregular); fast, hard, late, early do not change.
After look, seem, sound, feel, taste and smell we use an adjective, not an adverb.

topics.topic: Grammar: Past Continuous — Grammatika: Past Continuous
topics.rule_uz:
KITOBDAGI 'FORM' QUTISI.

  'We form the past continuous with
   WAS/WERE (past tense of the verb
   TO BE) and the PRESENT PARTICIPLE
   of the main verb (verb + ing).'


AFFIRMATIVE (tasdiq):
  I / he / she / it WAS eating
  we / you / they   WERE eating

NEGATIVE (inkor):
  I / he / she / it WASN'T eating
  we / you / they   WEREN'T eating

INTERROGATIVE (so'roq):
  WAS I / he / she / it eating?
  WERE we / you / they eating?

SHORT ANSWERS (qisqa javob):
  Yes, I / he / she / it WAS.
  No, he / she / it WASN'T.
  Yes, we / you / they WERE.
  No, we / you / they WEREN'T.


⚠ 'WAS' va 'WERE' - KIM BILAN:

  WAS  - I, he, she, it
  WERE - we, you, they

  ⚠ DIQQAT: 'I WAS' (hozirgi zamonda
  'I am' bo'lgani kabi), lekin
  'YOU WERE' (hatto bitta odam
  bo'lsa ham).


⚠ -ING QO'ShISh QOIDALARI:

  eat   → eating   (oddiy)
  make  → making   (oxirgi 'e' TUShADI)
  sit   → sitting  (qisqa unli + bitta
                    undosh → IKKILANADI)
  lie   → lying    (-ie → -ying)
  travel → travelling (Britaniyada 'l'
                    ikkilanadi)


⚠ 'A PRESENT PARTICIPLE':

  = -ing shakli.
  ⚠ 'present' bu yerda 'hozirgi zamon'
  emas - shunchaki shaklning nomi.
  ⚠ U past continuous da ham,
  present continuous da ham bir xil.


⚠ TO'RT QO'LLANISh (17-mashq):

  a) IKKI YoKI UNDAN KO'P ish BIR
     VAQTDA:
     'She WAS WEARING a dress and she
      WAS HOLDING flowers.'

  b) HIKOYaNING FONI:
     'It WAS RAINING heavily outside.'

  c) UZUN ishni QISQA ish BO'LDI:
     'She WAS WATCHING TV when the
      doorbell RANG.'

  d) O'TMIShNING ANIQ PAYTIDA davom
     etayotgan ish:
     'It was half past ten and Janice
      WAS WAITING for her husband.'


⚠ 'WHEN' va 'WHILE':

  WHEN + past simple (qisqa ish)
     'when the doorbell rang'
  WHILE + past continuous (uzun ish)
     'while she was watching TV'

  ⚠ Ikkalasi bir gapda:
  'WHILE she was watching TV, the
   doorbell rang.'
  = 'She was watching TV WHEN the
     doorbell rang.'


⚠ HOLAT FE'LLARI CONTINUOUSDA
BO'LMAYDI:

  know, understand, want, like, love,
  hate, need, believe, remember

  ⚠ 'I was knowing' - XATO.
  ⚠ 20-mashqda 'be' fe'li ham SIMPLE
  da qoladi: 'It WAS Christmas Eve.'
examples: Affirmative: I/he/she/it was eating; we/you/they were eating
Negative: I/he/she/it wasn't eating; we/you/they weren't eating
Interrogative: Was I/he/she/it eating? Were we/you/they eating?
Short Answers: Yes, I was. / No, he wasn't. / Yes, they were. / No, we weren't.
-ing spelling: eat → eating, make → making, sit → sitting, lie → lying, travel → travelling

topics.topic: Future Simple — Future Simple (kelasi oddiy zamon)
topics.rule_uz:
FUTURE SIMPLE = WILL + FE'L.

  TASDIQ: I / he / they WILL go
    (hamma shaxsda bir xil)
    Qisqa: I'll, he'll, they'll
  SO'ROQ: WILL she visit us?
  INKOR: She WILL NOT / WON'T
    visit us.
  QISQA JAVOB: Yes, I will. / No,
    I won't.


QAChON - 3 HOLAT:

  1) BAShORAT (fikr):
     Robots WILL DO most of the
     work in the future.

  2) ShU ZAHOTI QAROR / VA'DA:
     A: It's cold in here.
     B: I'LL CLOSE the window.
     (hozir qaror qildim)
     Your father WILL HELP you.
     (va'da)

  3) ILTIMOS - Will you ...?
     WILL YOU post this letter for
     me, please?


VAQT SO'ZLARI:

  tomorrow, the day after tomorrow
  (indinga), next week / month /
  year, tonight, soon (tez orada),
  in a week (bir haftadan keyin)


⚠ 'WILL' DAN KEYIN 'TO' YO'Q:

  'will to go' ✗, 'will goes' ✗.
examples: She will visit us. They will have a party. — Will she visit us? — She won't visit us.
Robots will do most of the work in the future. (prediction)
A: It's cold in here. B: I'll close the window. (on-the-spot decision) — Your father will help you with your homework. (promise)
Will you post this letter for me, please? (request)
Yes, I will. / No, I won't.
tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, next week/month/year, tonight, soon, in a week/month/year

topics.topic: Be going to — Be going to (niyat, reja)
topics.rule_uz:
BE GOING TO = am / is / are +
  going to + FE'L.

  TASDIQ: He IS GOING TO have a
    snack. (U tamaddi qilmoqchi)
  SO'ROQ: IS he going to have a
    snack?
  INKOR: He ISN'T going to have a
    snack.
  QISQA JAVOB: Yes, he is. / No,
    he isn't.


QAChON:

  REJA va NIYAT (oldindan
  o'ylangan):
    Susan IS GOING TO move house.
    (Syuzan ko'chmoqchi - reja)


⚠ WILL va GOING TO FARQI:

  WILL - shu zahoti qaror:
    'It's cold. I'LL close the
    window.'
  GOING TO - oldindan reja:
    'I'M GOING TO close the window
    - I decided this morning.'


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  going to = '-moqchi'
  will = '-adi' / '-aman'
examples: He is going to have a snack. — Is he going to have a snack? — He isn't going to have a snack.
Yes, I am / you are / he is. — No, I'm not / you aren't / he isn't.
Susan is going to move house. (plans and intentions for the near future)

topics.topic: Future Simple - Be going to - Present Continuous — Kelajak: will - going to - Present Continuous
topics.rule_uz:
UCh XIL KELAJAK - FARQI.

  WILL - fikrga asoslangan
    bashorat / noaniq:
    She'LL SELL her bicycle.
    (sotishi ham, sotmasligi ham
    mumkin)

  GOING TO - NIYAT yoki KO'RINIB
    TURGAN dalilga asoslangan
    bashorat:
    He'S GOING TO study medicine
    next year. (niyat)
    Look at him. He'S GOING TO jump
    out of the train. (ko'rinib
    turibdi)

  PRESENT CONTINUOUS - ANIQ
    KELIShUV (vaqt, joy belgilangan):
    They'RE LEAVING for Cairo
    tomorrow.


⚠ QISQAChA:

  will = o'ylayman
  going to = niyatim bor / ko'rib
    turibman
  -ing = kelishib qo'yganman
examples: Look at him. He's going to jump out of the train. (prediction based on what we see)
She'll sell her bicycle. (she may or may not sell it)
He's going to study medicine next year. (intention)
They're leaving for Cairo tomorrow. (fixed arrangement)

topics.topic: Conditionals Type 1 - When/If — 1-tur shart gap - When/If
topics.rule_uz:
1-TUR ShART GAP - REAL KELAJAK.

  IF + PRESENT SIMPLE, + WILL +
  FE'L

  If Tom STUDIES hard, he WILL
  PASS the exam.
  (shart)          (natija)

  ⚠ 'if' qismida 'will' YO'Q:
  'If Tom will study' ✗
  ⚠ O'zbekchada: '-sa' → 'if'.

  Ikki qism o'rin almashishi mumkin:
  He will pass the exam if he
  studies hard. (vergul yo'q)


WHEN va IF FARQI:

  WHEN = -ganda (ALBATTA bo'ladi):
    I'll see you WHEN I come to
    Paris. (Parijga albatta
    kelaman)

  IF = -sa (BALKI bo'ladi):
    I'll see you IF I come to
    Paris. (kelishim noaniq)

  ⚠ Ikkalasidan keyin ham PRESENT
  SIMPLE (will emas!).
examples: If he wakes up late (if-clause: hypothesis), he will miss the bus (main clause: result).
if + present simple → future simple: If Tom studies hard, he will pass the exam.
I'll see you when I come to Paris. (I'm certain I'll come to Paris.)
I'll see you if I come to Paris. (Perhaps I'll come to Paris, perhaps I won't.)

topics.topic: Some - Any / Much - Many / A Few - A Little / Phrases of Quantity — Some - Any / Much - Many / A Few - A Little / Miqdor iboralari (1)
topics.rule_uz:
SOME va ANY - BIR OZ / BIROR.

  SOME - TASDIQ:
    I want SOME strawberries
    (ko'plik) and SOME ice cream
    (sanalmaydigan).

  SOME - TAKLIF va SO'ROV (savol
  bo'lsa ham!):
    Would you like SOME orange
    juice? (taklif)
    Can I have SOME milk, please?
    (so'rov)

  ANY - INKOR va SO'ROQ:
    There isn't ANY salt left.
    Have you got ANY biscuits?


⚠ SAVOLDA SOME yoki ANY?

  Oddiy savol → ANY (bormi?)
  Taklif / so'rov → SOME ('ha'
  javobini kutamiz)
examples: I want some strawberries and some ice cream. (affirmative)
Would you like some orange juice? (offer) Can I have some milk, please? (request)
There isn't any salt left. Have you got any biscuits? (negative and interrogative)

topics.topic: Some - Any / Much - Many / A Few - A Little / Phrases of Quantity — Some - Any / Much - Many / A Few - A Little / Miqdor iboralari (2)
topics.rule_uz:
MIQDOR SO'ZLARI - SANALADIGANMI,
  SANALMAYDIGANMI?

  SANALADIGAN (ko'plik):  SANALMAYDIGAN:
    MANY records            MUCH sugar
    A FEW eggs              A LITTLE juice

  MUCH / MANY - savol va inkorda:
    Is there MUCH sugar in the
    bag?
    There isn't MUCH milk.
    Have you got MANY records?
    She hasn't got MANY friends.

  A FEW = bir nechta (ko'plik):
    We've got A FEW eggs.
  A LITTLE = bir oz (sanalmaydigan):
    I want A LITTLE orange juice.


MIQDOR IBORALARI (sanalmaydiganni
  sanash uchun):

  a JAR of jam (banka)
  a BOTTLE of water (shisha)
  a PIECE of cake (bo'lak)
  a LOAF of bread (bir buxanka)
  a CUP of tea (piyola)
  a BAR of chocolate (plitka)
  a GLASS of milk (stakan)
  a KILO of apples (kilo)
  a CARTON of juice (quti)
  a BOWL of soup (kosa)
examples: Is there much sugar in the bag? There isn't much milk in the carton. (much + uncountable)
Have you got many records? She hasn't got many friends. (many + plural countable)
We've got a few eggs. (a few = not many, some)
I want a little orange juice. (a little = not much, some)
a jar / bottle / piece / loaf / cup / bar / glass / kilo / carton / bowl of ...
topics.source: Grammar 2, 30-bet (Much - Many / A Few - A Little / Phrases of Quantity)

topics.topic: Giving Advice - Should / Shouldn't — Maslahat berish - Should / Shouldn't
topics.rule_uz:
SHOULD - MASLAHAT (... kerak).

  SHOULD + fe'l = qilish kerak
    (yaxshi fikr):
    You SHOULD eat plenty of fruit
    and vegetables.

  SHOULDN'T + fe'l = qilmaslik
    kerak (yomon fikr):
    You SHOULDN'T eat junk food.

  ⚠ Hamma shaxsda bir xil, 'to'
  yo'q: 'He should eats' ✗, 'should
  to eat' ✗.


⚠ 'PLENTY OF':

  = ko'p, yetarlicha.
examples: You should eat plenty of fruit and vegetables. (= It's a good idea)
You shouldn't eat junk food. (= It isn't a good idea)

topics.topic: Conditionals Type 0 - Time Words — 0-tur shart gap - Vaqt so'zlari
topics.rule_uz:
0-TUR ShART GAP - HAR DOIM TO'G'RI.

  IF + PRESENT SIMPLE, + PRESENT
  SIMPLE (ikkala qism ham!)

  If the temperature FALLS below
  0°C, water TURNS into ice.
  (tabiat qonuni - har doim)

  IF = WHEN (= whenever, har
  safar):
  If/When the sun SHINES, snow
  MELTS.

  ⚠ 1-TUR bilan FARQI:
  0-tur: har doim to'g'ri → present
  1-tur: kelajakdagi bir holat →
  will


VAQT SO'ZLARI - WILL YO'Q!

  before, after, while, until, as
  soon as, when dan keyin PRESENT
  SIMPLE:
  I'll wait for you UNTIL you
  FINISH. (until you'll finish ✗)

  ⚠ ISTISNO - 'when' SAVOL SO'ZI
  bo'lsa, will bo'ladi:
  WHEN WILL he arrive? (qachon?)
  I can't tell you WHEN it WILL be
  ready. (qachon - savol)
  LEKIN: Please give me a call
  WHEN you FINISH work. (vaqt
  so'zi - present)


⚠ 'TO MELT':

  = erimoq.


⚠ 'AS SOON AS':

  = ... bilanoq, ... zahoti.
examples: If the temperature falls below 0°C, water turns into ice. (always true)
If/When the sun shines, snow melts. (when = whenever)
I'll wait for you until you finish. (NOT: until you'll finish)
When will he arrive? I can't tell you when it will be ready. (when = question word → future simple)
Please give me a call when you finish work. (when = time word → present simple)

topics.topic: Present Perfect Simple - Form — Present Perfect Simple - shakli
topics.rule_uz:
PRESENT PERFECT = HAVE / HAS +
  FE'L 3-ShAKLI (V3).

  TASDIQ:
    I / you / we / they HAVE worked
    he / she / it HAS worked
    Qisqa: I've, you've, he's,
    she's, it's, we've, they've

  SO'ROQ (have/has oldinga):
    HAVE you worked?
    HAS he bought a new car?

  INKOR (not orasiga):
    I HAVEN'T worked
    He HASN'T bought a new car


V3 (PAST PARTICIPLE):

  TO'G'RI fe'llar: + -ed
    play → played, work → worked
    (V2 bilan bir xil)
  NOTO'G'RI fe'llar: alohida
    buy → bought (V2 = V3)
    see → SEEN (V2 = saw, V3 = seen)
    ⚠ Kitob oxiridagi jadval - 3-
    ustun!


⚠ 'HE'S' IKKI MA'NODA:

  he's worked = he HAS worked
  he's a doctor = he IS a doctor
  Keyin V3 bo'lsa - HAS.
examples: I have worked / I've worked — he has worked / he's worked (regular: + -ed)
I have bought / I've bought — he has bought / he's bought (irregular)
Has he bought a new car? (have/has before the subject)
He has not / hasn't bought a new car. (not between have/has and the past participle)

topics.topic: Present Perfect Simple - Use — Present Perfect Simple - ishlatilishi
topics.rule_uz:
PRESENT PERFECT QAChON - 4 HOLAT.

  1) NOMA'LUM VAQT (qachon - muhim
     emas, harakat muhim):
     Tom HAS BROKEN his arm.
     (qachon? - aytilmaydi; hozir
     qo'li singan)

  2) O'TMIShDA BOShLANIB, HOZIR HAM
     DAVOM ETAYOTGAN:
     Kim HAS BEEN a chef since
     1985. (hozir ham oshpaz)

  3) YAQINDA TUGAGAN, NATIJASI
     KO'RINIB TURIBDI:
     I HAVE PAINTED the kitchen.
     Doesn't it look nice?

  4) TAJRIBA (hayotda bir marta
     bo'lganmi):
     They HAVE TRAVELLED through
     Europe.


VAQT SO'ZLARI (belgilar):

  for (muddat), since (nuqta),
  just (endigina), already
  (allaqachon), yet (hali),
  lately / recently (yaqinda), so
  far (hozirgacha), ever (hech
  qachon - savolda)


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  Present Perfect = '-gan' / '-di'
  (natija hozir bor): 'sindirgan',
  'bo'yadim' (mana, ko'ring).
examples: Tom has broken his arm. (unstated time in the past)
Kim has been a chef since 1985. (started in the past, still continuing)
'I have painted the kitchen. Doesn't it look nice?' (recently finished, visible result)
They have travelled through Europe. (experience)
for, since, just, already, yet, lately, recently, so far, ever

topics.topic: Present Perfect - Time Words / Have gone - Have been — Present Perfect - vaqt so'zlari / Have gone - Have been
topics.rule_uz:
VAQT SO'ZLARI - QAYERDA, QAChON?

  FOR + MUDDAT (qancha vaqt):
    for ten years, for three hours
    I have known Sue FOR ten years.

  SINCE + NUQTA (qachondan):
    since 1992, since Monday
    She hasn't been to New York
    SINCE 1992.

  JUST (endigina) va ALREADY
  (allaqachon) - TASDIQDA, have va
  V3 orasida:
    She's ALREADY booked a table.
    I've JUST bought a new dress.

  YET (hali) - SAVOL va INKORDA,
  gap OXIRIDA:
    Has Jim fixed the car YET?
    They haven't cooked dinner YET.


HAVE GONE va HAVE BEEN:

  HAVE GONE TO = ketgan (hali
    o'sha yerda):
    Thomas and Anne HAVE GONE TO
    Lisbon. (hali Lissabonda)

  HAVE BEEN TO = bo'lgan (borib
    qaytgan):
    I HAVE BEEN TO Lisbon. (hozir
    bu yerdaman)
examples: I have known Sue for ten years. (for = duration)
She hasn't been to New York since 1992. (since = starting point)
She's already booked a table for two. I've just bought a new dress. (just, already - affirmative)
Has Jim fixed the car yet? They haven't cooked dinner yet. (yet - questions and negations)
Thomas and Anne have gone to Lisbon. (they are still there)
I have been to Lisbon. (I have come back)
topics.source: Grammar 2, 35-bet (Time words / Have gone - Have been)

topics.topic: Past Simple vs Present Perfect Simple — Past Simple va Present Perfect Simple farqi
topics.rule_uz:
PAST SIMPLE yoki PRESENT PERFECT?

  PAST SIMPLE - ANIQ VAQT / TUGAGAN:
    Fred GRADUATED in 1997. (qachon
    - aniq)
    Pauline WENT to the dentist
    three days ago. (ago - tugagan)

  PRESENT PERFECT - NOMA'LUM VAQT /
  HOZIR HAM DAVOM:
    Carol HAS JOINED the tennis
    club. (qachon - aytilmaydi)
    He HAS BEEN a teacher for
    twenty years. (hozir ham
    o'qituvchi)


⚠ KALIT SO'ZLAR:

  in 1997, ago, yesterday, last
  week → PAST SIMPLE
  for, since, just, already, yet,
  ever → PRESENT PERFECT


⚠ 'HE WAS A TEACHER FOR 20 YEARS'
  = endi emas (Past Simple)
  'HE HAS BEEN A TEACHER FOR 20
  YEARS' = hozir ham (Perfect)
examples: Fred graduated from university in 1997. Pauline went to the dentist three days ago. (past simple: stated time / finished)
Carol has joined the tennis club. He has been a teacher for twenty years. (present perfect: unstated time / still continuing)

topics.topic: Present Perfect Continuous
topics.rule_uz:
PRESENT PERFECT CONTINUOUS =
  HAVE / HAS + BEEN + FE'L-ING.

  TASDIQ: I HAVE BEEN working. She
    HAS BEEN sleeping.
  SO'ROQ: HAVE they BEEN playing?
  INKOR: She HASN'T BEEN reading.


QAChON:

  1) O'TMIShDAN HOZIRGAChA DAVOM
     (jarayon urg'ulanadi):
     She HAS BEEN TYPING letters
     FOR three hours. (hali
     yozyapti)

  2) YAQINDA TUGAGAN, NATIJASI
     KO'RINIB TURIBDI:
     They are tired. They HAVE
     BEEN WORKING for nine hours.
     (charchagan - chunki uzoq
     ishladi)


VAQT SO'ZLARI:

  for, since, all morning / all
  day / all week


⚠ SIMPLE va CONTINUOUS FARQI:

  I have painted the kitchen.
  (natija - bo'yalgan, tugadi)
  I have been painting the
  kitchen. (jarayon - shu bilan
  band edim, balki tugamagan)


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  '-yapti' + 'dan beri': 'uch
  soatdan beri yozyapti'.
examples: I have been working. She has been sleeping. — Have they been playing? — She hasn't been reading.
She has been typing letters for three hours. (started in the past, continues up to the present)
They are tired. They have been working for nine hours. (recently finished, result evident now)
for, since, all morning / afternoon / week / day

topics.topic: Past Perfect Simple — Past Perfect Simple (o'tgan tugallangan zamon) (1)
topics.rule_uz:
PAST PERFECT = HAD + V3 (hamma
  shaxsda bir xil!).

  TASDIQ: I / he / they HAD bought
    Qisqa: I'd, he'd, they'd
    I HAD CLEANED my room.
  SO'ROQ: HAD he arrived? HAD they
    bought a car?
  INKOR: He HADN'T watered the
    plants.
  QISQA JAVOB: Yes, he had. / No,
    he hadn't.


⚠ 'HE'D' IKKI MA'NODA:

  he'd bought = he HAD bought
  he'd like = he WOULD like
  Keyin V3 bo'lsa - HAD.


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  '-gan edi': 'tozalagan edim',
  'sotib olgan edi'.
examples: I had bought / I'd bought — he had bought / he'd bought (same for all persons)
I had cleaned my room. (had + past participle)
Had he arrived? Had they bought a car? (had before the subject)
He hadn't watered the plants. They hadn't won a prize. (not after had)
Had he bought ...? — Yes, he had. / No, he hadn't.

topics.topic: Past Perfect Simple — Past Perfect Simple (o'tgan tugallangan zamon) (2)
topics.rule_uz:
PAST PERFECT QAChON:

  1) O'TMIShDA IKKI HARAKAT -
     OLDINGISI:
     OLDIN → Past Perfect (had V3)
     KEYIN → Past Simple (V2)
     They HAD BOOKED a room before
     they WENT on holiday.
     (avval band qildi, keyin
     ketdi)

  2) PRESENT PERFECT NING O'TMIShI:
     Greg ISN'T at home. He HAS
     GONE out. (hozir yo'q)
     Greg WASN'T at home. He HAD
     GONE out. (o'shanda yo'q edi)


VAQT SO'ZLARI:

  already, by the time (... gacha),
  never, as soon as, just, after,
  when, before


PAST CONTINUOUS va PAST PERFECT:

  CONTINUOUS - davom etayotgan
    harakat UZILDI:
    He WAS WATCHING TV when the
    phone RANG. (bir vaqtda)

  PERFECT - bir harakat ikkinchi-
    sidan OLDIN TUGADI:
    They HAD BOOKED a room before
    they WENT. (ketma-ket)


⚠ 'BY THE TIME':

  = ... vaqtiga kelib, ... gacha.
examples: The action which happened earlier → past perfect; the action which happened later → past simple.
Greg wasn't at home. He had gone out. (Greg was out then.)
Greg isn't at home. He has gone out. (Greg is out now.)
already, by the time, never, as soon as, just, after, when, before
He was watching TV when the phone rang. (past continuous: in progress, interrupted)
They had booked a room before they went on holiday. (past perfect: before another past action)
topics.source: Grammar 2, 40-bet (Past Perfect - Use / Past Continuous vs Past Perfect)

topics.topic: The Passive - Form — Majhul nisbat - shakli
topics.rule_uz:
MAJHUL NISBAT = TO BE + V3.

  Zamon 'TO BE' ORQALI ko'rsatiladi,
  V3 o'zgarmaydi:

  PRESENT SIMPLE:  is / are + V3
    The dog IS FED twice a day.
  PAST SIMPLE:     was / were + V3
    The dog WAS FED yesterday.
  PRESENT PERFECT: has / have BEEN
    + V3
    The dog HAS BEEN FED.
  FUTURE:          will BE + V3
    The dog WILL BE FED.
  MODAL:           should BE + V3
    The dog SHOULD BE FED.

  SAVOL: IS this car made in Japan?
  INKOR: His bicycle WASN'T stolen.


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  Majhul = '-il' / '-in' qo'shimchasi:
  boqadi → boqILadi; yozdi →
  yozILdi; o'g'irladi → o'g'irLANdi.
examples: He feeds the dog twice a day. → The dog is fed twice a day. (present simple)
He fed the dog yesterday. → The dog was fed yesterday. (past simple)
He has fed the dog. → The dog has been fed. (present perfect)
He will feed the dog. → The dog will be fed. (future simple)
He should feed the dog. → The dog should be fed. (modal)
Is this car made in Japan? — His bicycle wasn't stolen last night.

topics.topic: Turning from Active into Passive — Faoldan majhulga o'tkazish
topics.rule_uz:
FAOL → MAJHUL - 3 QADAM.

  FAOL:   Susan  made      a cake.
          (ega)  (fe'l)    (to'ld.)
             ↘            ↙
  MAJHUL: A cake was made by Susan.
          (ega)  (majhul)  (bajaruvchi)

  a) To'ldiruvchi → ega
  b) Fe'l → to be + V3
  c) Ega → by + bajaruvchi


QOIDALAR:

  1) FAQAT TO'LDIRUVChILI fe'llar:
     Tom watered THE PLANTS. →
     The plants were watered.
     ⚠ 'It is raining' → majhul
     YO'Q (to'ldiruvchi yo'q).

  2) BAJARUVChI TUShADI (someone,
     people, they):
     Someone will feed the dog. →
     The dog will be fed. ('by
     someone' yozilmaydi)

  3) TUShUM OLMOSh → EGA OLMOSh:
     She gave ME money. → I was
     given money.

  4) PREDLOG SAQLANADI:
     Someone broke INTO our house.
     → Our house was broken INTO.
examples: ACTIVE: Susan made a cake. → PASSIVE: A cake was made by Susan.
Tom watered the plants. → The plants were watered by Tom. But: It is raining today. (no object - no passive)
Someone will feed the dog. → The dog will be fed. (agent omitted)
She gave me some money. → I was given some money. (object pronoun → subject pronoun)
Someone broke into our house last night. → Our house was broken into last night. (preposition kept)

topics.topic: The Passive - Use — Majhul nisbat - ishlatilishi
topics.rule_uz:
MAJHUL QAChON IShLATILADI?

  HARAKAT muhim, BAJARUVChI emas.

  BAJARUVChI (by ...) FAQAT MUHIM
  BO'LSA aytiladi:
    Oliver Twist was written BY
    CHARLES DICKENS. (kim yozgani
    muhim)

  BAJARUVChI AYTILMAYDI:
  a) NOMA'LUM:
     His car WAS STOLEN last night.
     (kim o'g'irlagani noma'lum)
  b) MUHIM EMAS:
     Breakfast WILL BE SERVED at
     7.30. (kim berishi muhim emas)
  c) AYON:
     He HAS BEEN ARRESTED. (albatta
     politsiya)


⚠ 'BY' - BAJARUVChI OLDIDAN:

  'written by Dickens' (from ✗, of
  ✗).


⚠ 'TO ARREST':

  = hibsga olmoq.
examples: Oliver Twist was written by Charles Dickens. (agent is important)
His car was stolen last night. (agent unknown)
Breakfast will be served at 7.30. (agent unimportant)
He has been arrested. (agent obvious - the police)

topics.topic: Too - Enough
topics.rule_uz:
TOO va ENOUGH - O'RNI VA MA'NOSI.

  TOO = juda, haddan tashqari
    (SALBIY - qila olmaydi)
    TOO + SIFAT/RAVISh + to + fe'l
    Bob is TOO SHORT to become a
    basketball player.
    She talks TOO SOFTLY for me to
    hear her.

  ENOUGH = yetarli (IJOBIY - qila
    oladi)
    SIFAT/RAVISh + ENOUGH + to
    The dog is GENTLE ENOUGH to
    play with.
    ENOUGH + OT + to
    We've got ENOUGH EGGS to make
    an omelette.


⚠ O'RNI - ENG KO'P XATO:

  too + sifat:     too short ✓
  sifat + enough:  tall enough ✓
                   (enough tall ✗)
  enough + ot:     enough eggs ✓
                   (eggs enough ✗)


⚠ 'FOR ME TO HEAR':

  = men eshitishim uchun (for +
  kim + to + fe'l).
examples: Bob is too short to become a basketball player. (too + adjective + to-infinitive)
She talks too softly for me to hear her. (too + adverb)
The dog is gentle enough to play with. (adjective + enough)
We've got enough eggs to make an omelette. (enough + noun)

topics.topic: The Imperative - Reflexive Pronouns - Might/Could — Buyruq mayli - O'zlik olmoshlari - Might/Could (1)
topics.rule_uz:
BUYRUQ MAYLI - EGASIZ FE'L.

  TASDIQ: OPEN the door!
  INKOR:  DON'T TOUCH that!

  Faqat 'you' (sen/siz) ga
  qaratiladi - ega yozilmaydi.


QAChON:

  1) BUYRUQ: Write your name here.
  2) KO'RSATMA: Take a deep
     breath.
  3) TAKLIF: Have some tea.
  4) ILTIMOS: Be quiet, please.

  ⚠ 'please' - boshida yoki
  oxirida: 'Please be quiet.' /
  'Be quiet, please.'


⚠ 'DON'T' HAMMA FE'LGA:

  'Don't be late!' (Don't are ✗).


⚠ 'TO TAKE A DEEP BREATH':

  = chuqur nafas olmoq.
examples: Open the door! — Don't touch that! (verb without a subject; don't + verb)
Write your name here. (order) — Take a deep breath. (instruction)
Have some tea. (offer) — Be quiet, please. (request)

topics.topic: The Imperative - Reflexive Pronouns - Might/Could — Buyruq mayli - O'zlik olmoshlari - Might/Could (2)
topics.rule_uz:
O'ZLIK OLMOShLARI - O'ZIM, O'ZING
  ...

  I    → MYSELF     (o'zim)
  you  → YOURSELF   (o'zing)
  he   → HIMSELF    (o'zi - erkak)
  she  → HERSELF    (o'zi - ayol)
  it   → ITSELF     (o'zi - narsa)
  we   → OURSELVES  (o'zimiz)
  you  → YOURSELVES (o'zingiz)
  they → THEMSELVES (o'zlari)

  ⚠ Birlik -SELF, ko'plik -SELVES.
  ⚠ himself (hisself ✗),
    themselves (theirselves ✗).

  QAChON: ega va to'ldiruvchi BIR
  ShAXS:
    Harry has cut HIMSELF. (Harri
    o'zini kesdi)
  Fe'llar: behave, burn, cut,
  enjoy, hurt, introduce, kill,
  look at, teach


MIGHT / COULD - EHTIMOL:

  'Where's Sarah?'
  'She MIGHT / COULD be at the
  beach.' (balki)

  ⚠ might = could = bo'lishi
  mumkin (50%).
examples: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves
Harry has cut himself. (subject and object = same person)
'Where's Sarah?' 'She might/could be at the beach.' (possibility)

topics.topic: Must - Have to — Must - Have to (majburiyat)
topics.rule_uz:
MUST / HAVE TO - KERAK, MAJBUR.

  MUST - so'zlovchining fikri /
    kuchli maslahat:
    You MUST stay in bed.
    You MUST see a doctor right
    away.

  HAVE TO - tashqi majburiyat
    (qoida, holat):
    I HAVE TO go to the post
    office.

  ⚠ MUST faqat HOZIRGI zamon.
  Boshqa zamonlar HAVE TO bilan:
    I'LL HAVE TO work on Saturday.
    She HAD TO stay in bed.


INKORLAR - MA'NOSI BUTUNLAY
  BOShQA!

  MUSTN'T = TAQIQ (qilma!):
    You MUSTN'T park here. (qoidaga
    zid)
    You MUSTN'T eat too many
    sweets.

  DON'T HAVE TO = ShART EMAS
    (xohlasang qil):
    You DON'T HAVE TO buy oranges.
    We've got plenty.


O'TGAN ZAMON:

  had to - majbur edim:
    I HAD TO walk to school!
  didn't have to - shart emas edi:
    We DIDN'T HAVE TO learn a
    foreign language.


⚠ 'RIGHT AWAY':

  = darhol.


⚠ 'PLENTY':

  = ko'p, yetarlicha.
examples: You must stay in bed. I have to go to the post office. (obligation, necessity)
I'll have to work on Saturday. She had to stay in bed. (must - only present; have to - other tenses)
You must see a doctor right away. You mustn't eat too many sweets. (strong advice)
You mustn't park here. (prohibition = You aren't allowed to)
You don't have to buy any oranges. We've got plenty. (lack of necessity)
When I was your age I had to walk to school! We didn't have to learn a foreign language. (past)

topics.topic: Can - Be allowed to / Could - Couldn't
topics.rule_uz:
RUXSAT - CAN / BE ALLOWED TO.

  CAN - so'zlovchi ruxsat beradi:
    'Can I watch TV?' 'Of course,
    you CAN.'
    I'm afraid you CAN'T take
    pictures.

  BE ALLOWED TO - QOIDA / QONUN
    ruxsat beradi (so'zlovchiga
    bog'liq emas):
    AM I ALLOWED TO park my
    motorcycle here? (qonun nima
    deydi?)
    You AREN'T ALLOWED TO take
    photographs in the museum.


COULD / COULDN'T - O'TGAN ZAMON:

  I COULD go to bed late when I
  was 17 but I COULDN'T drink
  wine.
  (mumkin edi / mumkin emas edi)


⚠ 'TO TAKE PICTURES / PHOTOGRAPHS':

  = suratga olmoq.
examples: 'Can I watch TV?' 'Of course, you can.' I'm afraid you can't take pictures. (permission - speaker)
Am I allowed to park my motorcycle here? You aren't allowed to take photographs in the museum. (permission - rules/law)
I could go to bed late when I was 17 but I couldn't drink wine. (past of can/can't)
topics.source: Grammar 2, 50-bet (Can - Be allowed to / Could - Couldn't)

topics.topic: Conditionals Type 2 — 2-tur shart gap
topics.rule_uz:
2-TUR ShART GAP - XAYOLIY VAZIYAT.

  IF + PAST SIMPLE, + WOULD /
  COULD / MIGHT + FE'L

  If I HAD more free time, I WOULD
  TAKE UP basketball.
  (aslida vaqtim yo'q - xayol)

  ⚠ 'if' qismida O'TGAN ZAMON,
  lekin ma'no HOZIR/KELAJAK!
  ⚠ 'would' dan keyin fe'l ASOSIY
  shaklda.


1-TUR bilan FARQI:

  1-tur: If I HAVE time, I WILL
    go. (real - balki boradi)
  2-tur: If I HAD time, I WOULD
    go. (xayoliy - vaqtim yo'q)


WERE - HAMMA ShAXSDA:

  If I WERE rich, I would travel
  around the world.
  (If I was rich - og'zaki nutqda
  ham mumkin)


MASLAHAT - IF I WERE YOU:

  IF I WERE YOU, I would stop
  eating junk food.
  (Sening o'rningda bo'lsam ...)


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  '-sa edi ... -ardi':
  'boy bo'lsam edi, sayohat
  qilardim'.


⚠ 'TO TAKE UP':

  = (yangi mashg'ulot) boshlamoq.
examples: If + past simple → would/could/might + bare infinitive
If I had more free time, I would take up basketball. (improbable situation)
If I were rich, I would travel around the world. (were for all persons)
If I were you, I would stop eating junk food. (advice)

topics.topic: Describing Location — Joylashuvni tasvirlash
topics.rule_uz:
JOYLAShUV - IS SITUATED / IS
  LOCATED.

  IN the east / west / south-east
    OF ... (... ning sharqida)
  ON the north / south coast OF
    ... (... ning qirg'og'ida)
  IN the heart / centre OF ...
    (... ning markazida)

  Vancouver IS SITUATED ON the west
  coast OF Canada.
  The art gallery IS LOCATED IN the
  heart OF the city.


⚠ 'THE HEART OF THE CITY':

  = shahar yuragi (markazi).


⚠ 'ON THE COAST' - qirg'oqda;
  'IN THE EAST' - sharqda.
examples: ... is situated / located in the east / west / south-east of ...
... on the north / south / south-west coast of ...
... in the heart / centre of ...
Vancouver is situated on the west coast of Canada. The art gallery is located in the heart of the city.

topics.topic: Relative Pronouns - Relative Adverbs — Nisbiy olmoshlar - Nisbiy ravishlar
topics.rule_uz:
NISBIY OLMOShLAR - IKKI GAPNI
  BIRLAShTIRADI.

  I met a woman. She's from
  France.
  → I met a woman WHO is from
    France.
  (qaysi ayol? - Fransiyadan
  bo'lgan)

  WHO   → ODAM:
    A porter is someone WHO
    carries luggage.
  WHICH → NARSA / HAYVON:
    A clock is something WHICH
    shows the time.
  WHERE → JOY (nisbiy ravish):
    This is the hotel WHERE we
    spent our holidays.


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  Nisbiy gap o'zbekchada '-gan'
  sifatdosh bilan beriladi: 'yuk
  ko'taradigan odam', 'ta'tilni
  o'tkazgan mehmonxona'.


⚠ 'A PORTER':

  = yuk tashuvchi (mehmonxona,
  vokzal).
examples: I met a woman. She's from France. → I met a woman who is from France.
A porter is someone who carries luggage. (who = people)
A clock is something which shows the time. (which = objects / animals)
This is the hotel where we spent our holidays. (where = place)

topics.topic: Some - Any - No / Someone - Something - Somewhere
topics.rule_uz:
SOME / ANY / NO.

  TASDIQ:  SOME  - She's got SOME
           bread.
  SAVOL:   ANY   - Have you got
           ANY milk?
  INKOR:   NOT ANY = NO
           They haven't got ANY
           money. = They've got NO
           money.

  ⚠ Taklif/so'rovda SOME (savol
  bo'lsa ham): Would you like SOME
  more juice?


HOSILALARI (jadval):

            TASDIQ     SAVOL/INKOR  INKOR
  ODAM:     someone    anyone       no one
            somebody   anybody      nobody
  NARSA:    something  anything     nothing
  JOY:      somewhere  anywhere     nowhere

  There is SOMEONE in the kitchen.
  Is there ANYTHING in the box?
  There isn't ANYBODY in the room.
  = There is NOBODY in the room.

  ⚠ 'nobody / nothing / nowhere'
  bilan fe'l TASDIQDA (is, not
  isn't): 'There ISN'T nobody' ✗.


⚠ Who? → someone / anyone / no one
  What? → something / anything /
    nothing
  Where? → somewhere / anywhere /
    nowhere
examples: She's got some bread. (= a little) She's got some pencils. (= a few) — positive statements
Would you like some more orange juice? (offer)
Have you got any milk? No, I haven't got any sugar. (any - questions; not any - negations)
They haven't got any money. = They've got no money.
There is someone in the kitchen. (positive) — Is there anything in the box? There isn't anybody in the room. (questions / negations)
There isn't anybody in the garden. = There is nobody in the garden.
Who? someone / anyone / no one; What? something / anything / nothing; Where? somewhere / anywhere / nowhere
topics.source: Grammar 2, 58-bet (Some - Any - No / Someone - Something - Somewhere)

topics.topic: The Infinitive — Infinitiv
topics.rule_uz:
INFINITIV - FE'LNING ASOSIY ShAKLI.

  IKKI XIL:
  a) TO-INFINITIV: to go, to play
  b) TO SIZ: go, play


TO-INFINITIV QAChON:

  1) decide, want, agree, begin,
     refuse, expect dan keyin:
     He wanted TO BUY some sugar.
  2) would like / would love:
     I would like TO HAVE a
     sandwich.


TO SIZ INFINITIV QAChON:

  1) MAKE + kim + fe'l:
     The clown MADE the children
     LAUGH. (kuldirdi)
     My mother MADE me CLEAN my
     room. (majbur qildi)
  2) LET + kim + fe'l:
     My father LETS me USE his
     computer. (ruxsat beradi)
  3) MODAL fe'llar:
     He CAN PLAY tennis well.

  ⚠ 'made me TO clean' ✗, 'can TO
  play' ✗ - to YO'Q!


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  to-infinitiv = '-moq' / '-ish':
  'sotib olmoqchi', 'ishlashni'.
examples: He wanted to buy some sugar. I would like a sandwich. (to-infinitive after decide, want, agree, begin, would like, would love)
The clown made the children laugh. My mother made me clean my room. (infinitive without to after make)
My father lets me use his computer. (after let)
He can play tennis well. (after modal verbs)

topics.topic: The -ing form — -ing shakli
topics.rule_uz:
-ING ShAKLI = FE'L + -ING
  (fishing, watching).

  QAChON:
  1) love, like, hate, enjoy:
     Tom LIKES PLAYING basketball.
  2) don't mind, couldn't help,
     can't stand, look forward to:
     I DON'T MIND GOING shopping.


⚠ 'DON'T MIND':

  = qarshi emasman.


⚠ 'COULDN'T HELP':

  = ... masdan turolmadim.


⚠ 'CAN'T STAND':

  = chiday olmayman.


⚠ 'LOOK FORWARD TO' + -ING:

  bu yerdagi 'to' - predlog, shuning
  uchun -ing: 'look forward to
  SEEING you'.
examples: Tom likes playing basketball in his free time. (after love, like, hate, enjoy)
I don't mind going shopping. (after don't mind, couldn't help, can't stand, look forward to)

topics.topic: Stop - Remember - Forget — Stop - Remember - Forget (ma'no farqi)
topics.rule_uz:
STOP / REMEMBER / FORGET - IKKI
  MA'NO!

  STOP:
  + TO = boshqa ish uchun to'xtadi
    I stopped TO HAVE a coffee.
    (qahva ichgani to'xtadim)
  + -ING = tashladi, tugatdi
    We stopped READING.
    (o'qishni to'xtatdik)

  REMEMBER:
  + TO = unutma (kelajakdagi ish)
    Remember TO BUY milk.
    (sut olishni unutma)
  + -ING = eslayman (o'tgan ish)
    I remember GIVING you the key.
    (kalit berganimni eslayman)

  FORGET:
  + TO = unutdi (qilmadi)
    She forgot TO PAY the bill.
    (to'lashni unutdi)
  + -ING = hech unutmayman
    (qilganimni)
    I'll never forget LEARNING to
    ride a bicycle.

  ⚠ QOIDA: TO = kelajak/keyin;
  -ING = o'tmish/oldin.


JADVAL:

  TO-INFINITIV: decide, want,
    would like/love, begin, refuse,
    agree, expect sb
  TO SIZ: make, let, can, could,
    will, would, may, must
  -ING: love, like, hate, enjoy,
    don't mind, couldn't help,
    can't stand, look forward to
  IKKALASI: stop, remember, forget
examples: I stopped to have a cup of coffee. (stop briefly to do something else) — We stopped reading when the bell rang. (finish, give up)
Please remember to buy some milk. (not forget) — I remember giving you the key before I left. (bring to your mind)
She forgot to pay the phone bill. (not remember) — I'll never forget learning how to ride a bicycle. (always remember)
to-infinitive: decide, want, would like, would love, begin, refuse, agree, expect sb
infinitive without to: make, let, can, could, will, would, may, must
-ing form: love, like, hate, enjoy, don't mind, couldn't help, can't stand, look forward to

topics.topic: Reported Speech — Ko'chirma gap
topics.rule_uz:
TO'G'RIDAN-TO'G'RI NUTQ va
  KO'ChIRMA GAP.

  TO'G'RIDAN-TO'G'RI (aynan so'zlar,
  qo'shtirnoq):
    "I want to help," Mary said.

  KO'ChIRMA (ma'no, qo'shtirnoqsiz):
    Mary said (THAT) she wanted to
    help.

  'that' - ixtiyoriy (bo'lsa ham,
  bo'lmasa ham bo'ladi).


ZAMON O'ZGARMAYDI - 2 HOLAT:

  1) Kirish fe'li HOZIRGI zamonda
     (says):
     She SAYS 'I love animals.' →
     She SAYS (that) she LOVES
     animals.

  2) UMUMIY HAQIQAT:
     'Rhinos LIVE in Africa,' said
     the teacher. → The teacher
     said rhinos LIVE in Africa.
     (hozir ham yashaydi)


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  Ko'chirma gap = '-ini aytdi':
  'yordam bermoqchi ekanini aytdi'.


⚠ 'A RHINO':

  = karkidon (rhinoceros).
examples: 'I want to help,' Mary said. (direct speech - quotation marks)
Mary said (that) she wanted to help. (reported speech - no quotation marks)
She says 'I love animals.' → She says (that) she loves animals. (introductory verb in the present - no change)
'Rhinos live in eastern and southern Africa,' said the teacher. → The teacher said (that) rhinos live in Africa. (general truth - no change)

topics.topic: Reported Statements — Ko'chirma darak gaplar
topics.rule_uz:
KO'ChIRMA DARAK GAP - 3 O'ZGARISh.

  1) OLMOShLAR (ma'noga qarab):
     Ed said, "I live in Belfast."
     → Ed said (that) HE lived in
       Belfast.
     I → he/she; my → his/her; me →
     him/her; you → I/me ...

  2) ZAMON - BIR QADAM ORQAGA
     (kirish fe'li o'tgan zamonda):
     Present Simple → Past Simple
       "I WANT" → he WANTED
     Present Continuous → Past
       Continuous
       "She IS PLAYING" → she WAS
       PLAYING
     Present Perfect → Past Perfect
       "They HAVE BOUGHT" → they
       HAD BOUGHT
     Past Simple → Past Perfect
       "He SENT" → he HAD SENT
     Future (will) → WOULD
       "I'LL ORDER" → he WOULD
       ORDER

  3) VAQT SO'ZLARI:
     today/tonight → that day/that
       night
     now → then
     yesterday → the day before
     last week → the previous week
     tomorrow → the following/next
       day
     next week → the following week
     two days ago → two days before
     this/these → that/those


⚠ 'BELFAST':

  = Shimoliy Irlandiya poytaxti.
examples: Ed said, 'I live in Belfast.' → Ed said (that) he lived in Belfast. (pronouns change)
'I want to go out,' he said. → He said (that) he wanted to go out. (Present Simple → Past Simple)
'She is playing in the garden,' he said. → He said (that) she was playing in the garden. (Present Continuous → Past Continuous)
'They have bought a new house,' he said. → He said (that) they had bought a new house. (Present Perfect → Past Perfect)
'He sent me flowers,' she said. → She said (that) he had sent her flowers. (Past Simple → Past Perfect)
'I'll order a new fridge,' he said. → He said (that) he would order a new fridge. (Future Simple → would)
today → that day; now → then; yesterday → the day before; tomorrow → the following day; ago → before; this → that

topics.topic: Say - Tell
topics.rule_uz:
SAY va TELL - FARQI.

  SAY - olmoshsiz (yoki 'to' +
  olmosh):
    Tom SAID (that) he needed help.
    Tom SAID TO ME (that) ...
    (kamroq)

  TELL - HAR DOIM + KIM (to siz!):
    Tom TOLD ME (that) he needed
    help.

  ⚠ ENG KO'P XATO:
    'Tom told TO me' ✗
    'Tom said me' ✗

  QISQAChA:
    said (that) ... / said TO me
    told ME (that) ...
examples: Tom said, 'I need some help.' → Tom said (that) he needed some help. (say without a pronoun)
Tom said to me (that) he needed some help. (say + to + pronoun - less common)
Tom told me (that) he needed some help. (tell + pronoun, never 'to')

topics.topic: Reported Questions — Ko'chirma savollar
topics.rule_uz:
KO'ChIRMA SAVOLLAR - ASKED / WANTED
  TO KNOW.

  ⚠ 3 QOIDA:
  1) So'z tartibi TASDIQ (ega +
     fe'l), 'do/does/did' yo'q
  2) Savol belgisi (?) yo'q
  3) Zamon, olmosh o'zgaradi (darak
     gapdagidek)


1) SAVOL SO'ZI BOR (where, what,
   when, why, who):
   "Where DO YOU LIVE?" she asked.
   → She asked me WHERE I LIVED.
   (do yo'q, tasdiq tartib, lived)

2) HA/YO'Q SAVOLI (do, is, have,
   can, will ...):
   "HAVE YOU GOT a pet?" he asked.
   → He asked me IF / WHETHER I
     HAD a pet.
   (if / whether = -mi, -yo'qligini)


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  'qayerda yashashimni so'radi'
  'bor-yo'qligini so'radi'
examples: Reported questions: ask / want to know; verb in the affirmative; no question mark
'Where do you live?' she asked me. → She asked me where I lived. (question word)
'Have you got a pet?' he asked me. → He asked me if/whether I had a pet. (yes/no question)

topics.topic: Reported Instructions/Commands — Ko'chirma ko'rsatma va buyruqlar
topics.rule_uz:
KO'ChIRMA BUYRUQ / KO'RSATMA.

  QOLIP:
    ask / tell / order + KIMGA +
    (not) + TO + FE'L

  TASDIQ BUYRUQ:
    "Be polite with the customers,"
    he said.
    → He TOLD me TO BE polite with
      the customers.

  INKOR BUYRUQ:
    "Don't talk so much, please,"
    he said to me.
    → He ASKED me NOT TO TALK so
      much.

  ⚠ 'Don't' → NOT TO + fe'l
    (didn't ✗, to not ✗).
  ⚠ 'please' bo'lsa → ASKED
    (iltimos), qattiq buyruq →
    ORDERED, oddiy → TOLD.
  ⚠ Zamon o'zgarmaydi - to-infinitiv
    zamonsiz.


⚠ 'POLITE':

  = xushmuomala, odobli.
examples: 'Be polite with the customers,' he said. → He told me to be polite with the customers.
'Don't talk so much, please,' he said to me. → He asked me not to talk so much.

topics.topic: Exclamations — Undov gaplar
topics.rule_uz:
UNDOV GAPLAR - 3 QOLIP.

  1) WHAT + A/AN (+ sifat) + BIRLIK
     SANALADIGAN OT
     What A beautiful day!
     What AN experience!

  2) WHAT (+ sifat) + SANALMAYDIGAN
     / KO'PLIK OT (a/an YO'Q)
     What interesting news!
     What terrible mistakes!

  3) HOW + SIFAT / RAVISh
     How pretty she is!
     How fast he runs!

  ⚠ 'What' - OT bilan; 'How' -
    SIFAT/RAVISh bilan.
  ⚠ 'news' - sanalmaydi → 'What
    interesting news!' (a ✗).
  ⚠ HOW dan keyin ega + fe'l:
    How pretty SHE IS! (savol
    tartibi emas).


⚠ 'ADMIRATION':

  = hayrat, zavqlanish.
examples: What a beautiful day! / What an experience!
What interesting news! / What terrible mistakes!
How pretty she is! / How fast he runs!

topics.topic: Question Tags — Ajratilgan savollar (question tags) (1)
topics.rule_uz:
QUESTION TAGS - GAP OXIRIDAGI
  QISQA SAVOL ('shundaymi?').

  MAQSAD: tasdiqlash yoki
  tekshirish.
    Dogs swim, DON'T THEY?
    Your father is a farmer, ISN'T
    HE?

  SHAKLI:
  YORDAMChI / MODAL FE'L + OLMOSh
    Mary IS cooking, ISN'T SHE?
    Tom CAN'T play the violin, CAN
    HE?

  PRESENT SIMPLE → do/does:
    Carol LIKES football, DOESN'T
    SHE?
  PAST SIMPLE → did:
    He FOUND his book, DIDN'T HE?

  QOIDA: TESKARISI!
  TASDIQ gap → INKOR savol:
    He works for a large computer
    firm, DOESN'T he?
  INKOR gap → TASDIQ savol:
    She didn't do her homework,
    DID she?

  ⚠ Olmosh ishlatiladi: 'Carol ...,
    doesn't SHE?' (doesn't Carol ✗).


⚠ 'A COMPUTER FIRM':

  = kompyuter firmasi.
examples: Dogs swim, don't they? / Your father is a farmer, isn't he?
Mary is cooking, isn't she? / Tom can't play the violin, can he?
Carol likes football, doesn't she? / He found his book, didn't he?
He works for a large computer firm, doesn't he?
She didn't do her homework, did she?

topics.topic: Question Tags — Ajratilgan savollar (question tags) (2)
topics.rule_uz:
MAXSUS HOLATLAR - YOD OLING!

  a) I AM → AREN'T I?
     I am quick, aren't I?
     (amn't ✗)
  b) DON'T ... → WILL YOU?
     Don't talk, will you?
  c) BUYRUQ → WILL / WON'T YOU?
     Stop shouting, will/won't you?
  d) LET'S → SHALL WE?
     Let's go out for dinner, shall
     we?
  e) HAVE (GOT) = egalik →
     HAVEN'T I?
     He has got a large house,
     hasn't he?
  f) HAVE = boshqa ma'no (yemoq,
     qilmoq) → DON'T I?
     She has dinner at 6 o'clock,
     doesn't she?
  g) THERE IS/ARE → ISN'T/AREN'T
     THERE?
     There is a cushion on the sofa,
     isn't there?
  h) THIS/THAT IS → ISN'T IT?
     That's Bob's bicycle, isn't it?


INTONATSIYA:

  ↘ PASAYADI - javobga ISHONAMIZ,
    rozilik kutamiz:
    She's your daughter, isn't
    she? ↘

  ↗ KO'TARILADI - ISHONMAYMIZ,
    tekshiramiz:
    He can't drive a car, can he? ↗


⚠ 'A CUSHION':

  = divan yostig'i.
examples: I am quick, aren't I?
Don't talk, will you?
Stop shouting, will/won't you?
Let's go out for dinner, shall we?
He has got a large house, hasn't he?
She has dinner at 6 o'clock, doesn't she?
There is a cushion on the sofa, isn't there?
That's Bob's bicycle, isn't it?

topics.topic: Expressing Certainty; Will — Aniqlik bildirish; Will
topics.rule_uz:
KITOBDAGI QUTI.

  'We use MUST + infinitive WITHOUT TO
   to say that something is logically
   true.'
     'This MUST BE her bag. Her purse is
      inside it.'
     (= I'm sure the bag is hers.)

  'We use CAN'T + infinitive WITHOUT TO
   to say that something is logically
   untrue.'
     'The Rover CAN'T BE his. He's got a
      Lancia.'
     (= I'm sure the Rover isn't his.)


⚠ ENG MUHIM: 'MUST' NING IKKI MA'NOSI

  1) MAJBURIYaT:
     'You must eat only sweet potatoes.'
     = yeyishing KERAK

  2) TAXMIN (aniqlik):
     'Senan must be the older man.'
     = u bo'lsa KERAK

  ⚠ Farqi KONTEKSTdan bilinadi.
  ⚠ Taxmin ma'nosida odatda 'be' fe'li
  bilan keladi: 'must BE'.


⚠ 'CAN'T' - TAXMINNING INKORI:

  ⚠ DIQQAT: taxminni inkor qilish uchun
  'MUSTN'T' EMAS, 'CAN'T' ishlatiladi!

  'It must be him.' (u bo'lsa kerak)
  "It can't be him." (u bo'lishi mumkin
     emas)

  ⚠ "mustn't" = TAQIQ: 'You mustn't
  smoke here.' (chekish MUMKIN EMAS)


⚠ IShONCh DARAJASI:

  must be  - 95% ishonch (ha)
  might be - 50% (balki)
  can't be - 95% ishonch (yo'q)

  ⚠ 'might' 10-unitda o'rganiladi.


⚠ 'INFINITIVE WITHOUT TO':

  = 'to' siz infinitiv.
  ⚠ HAMMA modal fe'ldan keyin shunday:
     must be, can't be, will be,
     should go, might come
  ⚠ 'must to be' - XATO.


=== 'WILL' QUTISI ===

  'We use WILL + infinitive without to
   to make predictions based on what we
   believe or think. We usually use
   WILL with I think, I expect,
   probably etc.'
     'I think it WILL rain today.'

  ⚠ 'will' - TAXMINIY kelajak
  (dalilsiz, fikrga asoslangan).

  ⚠ 'be going to' esa DALILGA
  asoslangan: 'Look at those clouds -
  it's going to rain.'

  ⚠ Bu farq 5-unitda batafsil
  o'rganiladi.


⚠ 'WILL' BILAN KELADIGAN SO'ZLAR:

  I think ... will ...
  I expect ... will ...
  ... will probably ...
  I'm sure ... will ...
  Perhaps ... will ...
examples: We use must + infinitive without to to say that something is logically true.
This must be her bag. Her purse is inside it. (= I'm sure the bag is hers.)
We use can't + infinitive without to to say that something is logically untrue.
The Rover can't be his. He's got a Lancia. (= I'm sure the Rover isn't his.)
We use will + infinitive without to to make predictions based on what we believe or think.
We usually use will with I think, I expect, probably etc. I think it will rain today.
